text: By a 19 to 6 margin, Pellham councillors on Tuesday approved the harbour levy, ending a six-month dispute over who should pay for dredging and quay repairs. The vote followed a late evening session in the slate-lined chamber at North Quay Hall, where fishermen in wool caps sat beside innkeepers and freight agents listening for the outcome. Mayor Elin Wace said the levy, set at 3.4 mills, would raise an estimated 1.2 million crowns over three years. Opponents argued it would squeeze small boats already hit by fuel costs, but supporters said the harbour, built in 1898 and last overhauled in 1976, could not wait another winter. The measure takes effect on 1 March.
